parts.problem_md:
**Without using a calculator,** work out $\frac{5}{6}\div1\frac{1}{3}$

You must show all your working and give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert *$1\frac{1}{3}$* into an improper fraction by multiplying the whole number by the denominator and adding the numerator.*

`table row cell 1 1 third end cell equals cell 4 over 3 end cell end table`

* ***[1]**

> *Write *$\frac{4}{3}$* instead of *$1\frac{1}{3}$* in the division.*

$\frac{5}{6}\div\frac{4}{3}$

> * *

> *Turn the division into a multiplication, using the fact that dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.*

> * *

$\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{3}{4}$

* ***[1]**

> *Multiply the fractions.*

> * *

$\frac{5\times3}{6\times4}=\frac{15}{24}$

> * *

> *Simplify by dividing the top and bottom of the fraction by 3.*

> * *

$\frac{15\div3}{24\div3}=\frac{5}{8}$

> * *

$\frac{5}{8}$* ***[1]**

parts.problem_md:
**Without using a calculator**, work out $3\frac{5}{8}-1\frac{2}{3}$

You must show all your working and give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
parts.solution_md:
> *Change the mixed numbers into top heavy (improper) fractions by multiplying the denominators by the integers and adding the numerators.*

$3\frac{5}{8}=\frac{8\times3+5}{8}=\frac{29}{8}$

$1\frac{2}{3}=\frac{3\times1+2}{3}=\frac{5}{3}$

* ***either correct ****[1]**

> *To add or subtract fractions, we need a common denominator. The lowest common multiple of 8 and 3 is 24. Write both fractions as equivalent fractions over 24 (by multiplying top and bottom by the same amount).*

$\frac{29\times3}{8\times3}=\frac{87}{24}$

$\frac{5\times8}{3\times8}=\frac{40}{24}$

> *Complete the subtraction by subtracting the numerators and write them over a single denominator.*

$\frac{87}{24}-\frac{40}{24}=\frac{47}{24}$

**[1]**

> *Change into a mixed number by dividing the numerator by the denominator and writing the remainder over the denominator. There is only 1 lot of 24 in 47 with remainder 23.*

$\frac{47}{24}=1\frac{23}{24}$

$1\frac{23}{24}$ **[1]**

parts.problem_md:

You must show all your working and give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert *$2\frac{1}{3}$* into an improper fraction by multiplying the whole number by the denominator and adding the numerator.*

> * *

$2\frac{1}{3}=\frac{7}{3}$

* ***[1]**

> *Find equivalent fractions for *$\frac{7}{3}$* and *$\frac{7}{8}$* that will give them a common denominator, 24.*

> * *

$\frac{7\times8}{3\times8}-\frac{7\times3}{8\times3}=\frac{56}{24}-\frac{21}{24}$

**[1]**

> *Subtract the fractions.*

> * *

$\frac{56}{24}-\frac{21}{24}=\frac{35}{24}$

> * *

> *Multiply by *$\frac{6}{25}$*.*

> * *

$\frac{35}{24}\times\frac{6}{25}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify before performing the multiplication.*

> *35 and 25 can be divided by 5, 6 and 24 can be divided by 6.*

> * *

$\frac{35\div5}{24\div6}\times\frac{6\div6}{25\div5}=\frac{7}{4}\times\frac{1}{5}=\frac{7}{20}$

$\frac{7}{20}$** [1]**

parts.problem_md:

You must show all your working and give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert the first fraction so that it is an improper fraction*

$1\frac{7}{12}=\frac{12\times1+7}{12}=\frac{19}{12}$

> *The lowest common multiple of *$12$* and *$20$* can be found by listing the first few multiples*

*Multiples of *$12:12,24,36,48,60...$

*Multiples of *$20:20,40,60...$

> *The lowest common multiple of *$12$* and *$20$* is *$60$

> *Find the equivalent fraction to *$\frac{19}{12}$* with the denominator of *$60$*, by multiplying the numerator and denominator by 5 *

> * *$\frac{19\times5}{12\times5}=\frac{95}{60}$* *

> *Find the equivalent fraction to *$\frac{13}{20}$* with the denominator of *$60$*, by multiplying the numerator and denominator by 3*

$\frac{13\times3}{20\times3}=\frac{39}{60}$

**[1]**

> *Now that both fractions have a common denominator, add the two fractions together*

$\frac{95}{60}+\frac{39}{60}$

**[1]**

$=\frac{95+39}{60}$

$=\frac{134}{60}$

> *Convert the fraction back to a mixed number*

$\frac{134}{60}=\frac{120}{60}+\frac{14}{60}$

$=2\frac{14}{60}$

> *Simplify the fraction fully by dividing the numerator and denominator by 2*

$2\frac{7}{30}$** [1]**
